subject: paper:rommelse-2010-shared-heritability
quote: Evidence indicates both disorders co-occur with a high frequency, in 20-50% of children with ADHD meeting criteria for ASD and in 30-80% of ASD children meeting criteria for ADHD.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Quantifies the bidirectional co-occurrence — the empirical basis for treating ADHD/ASD overlap as substantial, not incidental.

subject: paper:rommelse-2010-shared-heritability
quote: family and twin studies do provide support for the hypothesis that ADHD and ASD originate from partly similar familial/genetic factors.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The etiological claim: co-occurrence is underwritten by partly shared genetic origins, not only overlapping symptoms.

subject: paper:antshel-russo-2019
quote: ASD and ADHD have shared genetic heritability and are both associated with shared impairments in social functioning and executive functioning.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Independent statement of shared heritability plus shared social/executive impairment — the neurocognitive layer of the shared substrate.

subject: paper:antshel-russo-2019
quote: The research on ASD and ADHD suggests some overlap between the two disorders yet enough differences to indicate that these conditions are sufficiently distinct to warrant separate diagnostic categories.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. The counterweight: overlap does not erase the clinical distinction — the two remain separate categories.

subject: paper:leitner-2014
quote: The DSM-IV had specified that an ASD diagnosis is an exclusion criterion for ADHD, thereby limiting research of this common clinical co-occurrence.
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract. Documents the historical DSM-IV bar on dual diagnosis (lifted in DSM-5) and names the co-occurrence as common — context for why the overlap was under-studied.

subject: paper:leitner-2014
quote: both ASD and ADHD share some phenotypic similarities, but are characterized by distinct diagnostic criteria.
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract. Corroborates that phenotypic similarity coexists with distinct diagnostic criteria — supporting the distinct-categories reading.
